pattern: Composite structure behind a narrow interface: combine a hash map (find) with an ordered structure (who goes next), hide both behind a small Cache interface, put the 'who goes next' rule in a policy object, and add cross-cutting concerns (locking, stats, callbacks) as wrappers or striped segments rather than inside the core.

tips.nudge: What do callers do with a cache?
tips.hint: Write the two basic operations as functional requirements.
tips.show: F1: get(key) returns the value or a miss; put(key, value) inserts or updates.

tips.hint: State the size limit and when it is set.
tips.show: F2: Capacity is fixed at construction (e.g. 10,000 entries).

tips.nudge: It is full and a new key arrives. What happens?
tips.hint: Say which entry leaves and that the rule may change.
tips.show: F3: When full, put evicts the least-recently-used entry (rule pluggable: LFU, TTL later).

tips.nudge: The interviewer said who calls this.
tips.hint: Add a non-functional requirement about simultaneous callers.
tips.show: N2: Safe under dozens of concurrent threads, ~90% reads, without a global bottleneck.

tips.nudge: What does a caller call to read?
tips.hint: An operation taking a key and returning the value or a miss marker.
tips.show: Cache.get(key: K) -> V | None (marks the entry as most recently used).

tips.nudge: What does a caller call to write?
tips.hint: An operation taking key and value, possibly evicting.
tips.show: Cache.put(key: K, value: V) -> None (evicts per policy when full).

tips.nudge: How do you find a key in O(1)?
tips.hint: Name the structure that maps keys to entries.
tips.show: index: dict[K, Node] (key → node in the recency list).

tips.nudge: How do you know who is oldest, and move an entry to 'newest', in O(1)?
tips.hint: Name a structure where you can unlink any element and append in constant time.
tips.show: Doubly linked list of Node(key, value, prev, next) with sentinel head/tail; head = most recent.

tips.nudge: Callers should not care whether it is LRU, LFU or thread-safe.
tips.hint: Add an interface with just the operations callers need.
tips.show: interface Cache[K, V] { get; put; delete; size } implemented by LRUCache and wrappers.

tips.nudge: One team wants LFU next quarter.
tips.hint: Put 'which entry leaves' behind its own interface that the cache calls on access/insert/evict.
tips.show: interface EvictionPolicy { on_access(key); on_insert(key); victim() -> key } ← LRUPolicy, LFUPolicy.

tips.nudge: What does the map point to?
tips.hint: A small class that holds key, value and links.
tips.show: class Node { key, value, prev, next } (key is needed to delete from the map on eviction).

tips.nudge: Does the cache know which policy it runs, or only its interface?
tips.hint: Draw the concrete cache implementing the cache interface and using the policy interface.
tips.show: LRUCache implements Cache and uses EvictionPolicy; ThreadSafeCache implements Cache and wraps any Cache.

tips.nudge: A list alone is O(n) to find; a map alone has no order.
tips.hint: Combine two structures and say what each one is for.
tips.show: Hash map key → node + doubly linked list ordered by recency: get = lookup + move to head, put = insert at head + pop tail when full, all O(1).

tips.nudge: get moves a node, so even reads write. What does that do to a read-write lock?
tips.hint: Compare one global lock, a read-write lock, and splitting the cache into independently locked segments.
tips.show: Segmented (striped) cache: N segments by hash(key) % N, each an LRUCache with its own mutex; recency is approximate globally but contention drops ~N×. A read-write lock does not help because get mutates order.

tips.nudge: LFU, TTL and stats are all coming. Where do they go?
tips.hint: Explain how new policies and cross-cutting features plug in, and how contention scales.
tips.show: New rules = new EvictionPolicy; TTL = expiry check on get + policy; stats/callbacks = decorator or listener; more threads = more segments.

tips.nudge: Have you written the interface, the implementation, the node, the policy and both operations?
tips.hint: Declare the classes and the two operations with type hints.
tips.show: class Cache(ABC, Generic[K, V]): get(key) -> V | None; put(key, value). class LRUCache(Cache). class Node. class EvictionPolicy(ABC).
